text:
brandon_release: Heads-up — I'm pinning runtime v2.3.1 for model=redwood-base-1 on hosted for the next change window. Reason: observed token-level divergence after runtime 2.4.0 in internal evals. Will unpin after SDK 1.5.0 + runtime patch.

maya_dev: tagging @kevin_ops and @sasha_ml — what compat issues should we call out in release notes?

sasha_ml: tl;dr: 2.4.0 changed KV cache eviction timing + attention kernel reorder. Models using prefix caching + quantized 4-bit occasionally return truncation artifacts. Not frequent but shows up on long chat sessions (>2048 tokens).

kevin_ops: noted. Can we do a graceful fallback instead of full pin? e.g. route sensitive customers to runtime v2.2.x and others to 2.4?

brandon_release: thought about that — routing would help, but we don't have per-customer routing rules for hosted yet for model variants. Easier to pin at platform level for the short window.

julie_prod: change window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC works for most customers. If we pin now, we should publish a compatibility note + SDK advisory. Ops, can you confirm there won't be infra churn during that window?

kevin_ops: confirmed no infra maintenance in that window. We'll schedule the pin at 02:10 UTC and monitor. We'll keep canary at 5% for 15m once unpin happens.

deploy-bot: [deployment] created rollout 8132: pin runtime=2.3.1 -> applied to hosted pool alpha (read-only)

brandon_release: draft compatibility blurb (please quick-edit):
```
Compatibility note: We are pinning the inference runtime to 2.3.1 for the redwood-base-1 model on hosted while we investigate accuracy regressions introduced in runtime 2.4.0. Customers using SDK < 1.5.0 may observe subtle output changes if they upgrade runtime before SDK compatibility is confirmed. We recommend holding SDK updates until SDK 1.5.0 (expected next week) and avoiding runtime 2.4.0 for production workloads requiring long-context continuity.```

sasha_ml: add that quantized 4-bit workflows are most affected — and that this is not a model weight issue (no model re-publish needed).

brandon_release: good point, added.

maya_dev: quick question: do we need to pin model version too? My testing shows redwood-base-1@v2026-03-10 is fine, it's the runtime change.

brandon_release: not pinning model weights, only runtime. Will note in thread.

runtime-bot: [test-suite] regression tests: kv-cache-long-context FAILED x3 on runtime 2.4.0 (seed 42). Full logs: https://ci/reports/8132/kv-cache-long-context

kevin_ops: thanks @runtime-bot — that matches what we saw in canary last night. Plan: pin, publish advisory, run expanded test matrix on 2.4.0, then unpin + canary once runtime patch is out.

julie_prod: for release notes: include rollback instructions. Sample rollback command: `rwctl runtime set-version --model redwood-base-1 --version 2.3.1`

brandon_release: adding release-note checklist: [x] Pin runtime on hosted, [x] Post compatibility note, [x] Notify support, [ ] Publish SDK 1.5.0 advisory, [ ] Run extended regressions on 2.4.0

maya_dev: FYI I'm adding a small compatibility test to sdk-integration that checks decoding parity with runtime 2.3.1 vs 2.4.0 for long prompts. Will link results here when done.

deploy-bot: [deployment] rollout 8132: pinned runtime=2.3.1 -> success on 100% hosted pools (applied 02:10 UTC) :white_check_mark:

kevin_ops: monitoring metrics now. Alert if error-rate >2% or token-latency regresses >25th percentile.

brandon_release: we'll unpin after SDK 1.5.0 release + runtime 2.4.x patch. Targeting unpin next Tue during the same window. If anyone sees customer impact, please escalate here.

sasha_ml: adding note for docs: "If you rely on long KV cached sessions and use 4-bit quantization, prefer runtime <=2.3.1 for now."

maya_dev: posted test results: parity fails reproduced 3/10 seeds — attaching logs to the ticket.

brandon_release: thanks all. I'll do the external advisory + support template now. :thumbsup:
